Subject: VAT treatment for mixed billing and self-bill proposal

Hi Mina,

Quick question on tax handling as we get to contract: OrchidPay invoices customers for a platform subscription (recurring flat fee) plus variable usage fees (transaction-based). For EU customers who are VAT-registered, our accounting team wants to implement a single self-billing flow where OrchidPay issues consolidated invoices that show subscription and usage lines.

Can Redwood confirm whether the subscription + usage can be issued on a consolidated self-bill invoice with reverse-charge applied (VAT zeroed, buyer-supplied VAT IDs), or whether we need to split subscription vs usage into separate invoices due to place-of-supply rules? We have customers in Ireland, Germany and the Netherlands with mixed consumption profiles.

Also: attached is our proposed self-bill agreement (orchid-selfbill-proposal.pdf) and a sample VIES query screenshot for one buyer (vies-screenshot.png). What evidence do you need from our side to validate buyer VAT IDs and support reverse-charge handling?

Thanks — can we aim to resolve before the PO is signed next week?

Regards,
Liam O'Connor

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments.

Short answer: we can support a consolidated invoice in many EU-to-EU B2B cases, but whether reverse-charge (0% VAT) is appropriate for both lines depends on the place-of-supply rules for each line and on evidence we can validate for buyer VAT registration.

To make this operational and to avoid downstream payment holds, could you confirm the following so we can validate and document the treatment?
- Which legal entity of OrchidPay will sign the PO (country + VAT ID)?
- Are the affected end buyers VAT-registered companies (we need company VAT IDs and country codes) — sample list attached is fine.
- Can you confirm whether the usage fee is billed for a service 'consumed in the buyer's establishment' or is it tied to the seller's place (e.g., marketplace intermediary)?

I'll loop in tax/finance internally and return an actionable checklist and a draft consolidated invoice template. If convenient, we'll aim to get this to you by EOD Fri (June 26).

Hi — quick guidance from Tax Ops after a brief review. Long version below; TL;DR: consolidated invoice is acceptable in most EU B2B scenarios if we can validate buyer VAT IDs and document place-of-supply determination for each line. For usage lines where consumption location could vary, insist on buyer confirmation and evidence.

Checklist (what we need from OrchidPay to avoid payment hold and enable reverse-charge):
1) Signed self-billing agreement (seller + buyer signature) — confirms buyer accepts self-billing and responsibility for VAT reporting where applicable.
2) Buyer VAT number (with country prefix) + legal registered name + registered address that matches VAT registry.
3) Evidence of VAT registration: VIES screenshot is useful but we also want a registry extract or tax authority confirmation for IE/DE/NL for customers over a threshold.
4) Clear invoice fields: show buyer VAT number, buyer legal name, buyer address, line-level descriptions, unit amounts, and an explicit reference to "reverse charge — VAT accounted for by recipient" where applicable.
5) Where place-of-supply for usage could be seller's country or buyer's establishment, buyer must certify (email or contract clause) that consumption occurs in buyer's establishment.
6) Mapping table: which legal entity will receive payment (OrchidPay EU entity) and which billing entity Redwood should record.

Operational suggestions:
- Use single consolidated invoice template with per-line metadata (supply country code, VAT treatment tag). That lets our invoice parser route correctly.
- If buyer cannot provide registry extract, flag as "manual review" and hold reverse-charge until cleared.

Timeline: can produce a sanitized draft invoice template and a short evidence checklist by EOD Fri (June 26) if Mina okays.

Hi Liam — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and action items from our side. Please see the attached draft invoice template (draft-invoice-lineitems.csv) and our comments on the self-bill proposal.

What Redwood needs from OrchidPay to support reverse-charge on a consolidated invoice:
- Signed self-billing agreement (PDF). We reviewed your orchid-selfbill-proposal.pdf; if you can sign and return we will attach to the customer record.
- For each buyer to be treated under reverse-charge: 
  * Buyer VAT ID (with country prefix)
  * Buyer legal name and registered address (must match VAT registry)
  * A copy of registry extract or equivalent proof for IE/DE/NL (VIES screenshot is okay as a first pass but we need a registry extract for higher-value accounts)
  * For usage lines: a short statement (email is fine) from the buyer certifying consumption occurs at buyer's establishment or that buyer will self-account for VAT.
- Confirm which OrchidPay legal entity will be the invoicing party (country + VAT ID).

We will:
- Accept a consolidated invoice template that includes per-line metadata for place-of-supply and a VAT treatment tag (we attached a CSV with column examples).
- Run automated VIES checks against the supplied VAT IDs. Any mismatches will be escalated for manual review (we'll flag in our portal and notify your finance contact).
- Hold payment only if buyer evidence is missing — in which case we'll notify you and propose a 7-business-day remediation window.

Next steps / timeline:
1) You sign and return the self-bill agreement (or confirm you want Redwood to keep a signed copy on file) — target: Wed, Jun 30.
2) Provide a first batch of buyers (VAT IDs + registry extracts) for validation — target: Tue, Jun 29.
3) We will validate and return a status report and a sanitized draft invoice template for your billing system — target: Fri, Jul 2.

If that works, I'll mark the deal readiness steps in the CRM and set a short playbook for invoice parsing.
